question: Does the best of K=4 deterministic pass-1 orders (Java order, Q07 conflict-rounds, Q07 inside-out, seeded shuffle 1), optionally with 2 squeaky-wheel restarts, leave fewer KiCad-unconnected items than the default passes at no more than 1.5x their work on at least N-1 eligible boards, with none worse, no new DRC errors and no via in a pad?
rule_text: each pair is judged by N02's totals rule (freerouting-dev gate --prereg on a records file per pair): hard metrics 0, guards not worse than the pair's baseline, no board worse than twice its band, and the summed signal improved by more than the set noise; pass_rule (the paired rule) is printed for each pair, not judged

mp1.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, the same build as Q11.json's amendment 1, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
mp1.what: baseline: pass 1 only (Java's item order); amendment 1: the command of Q11.json's mp1 (with the report-only rip stats), so one run serves both registrations

mpdef.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, the same build as Q11.json's amendment 1, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
mpdef.what: baseline: the default passes; the work reference

portfolio4.engine: freerouting-rs release CLI of main at the run (amendment 1; one Linux build for every arm, the same build as Q11.json's amendment 1, its --version git sha in the note); the default profile
portfolio4.what: candidate: best of 4 pass-1 orders (configured = Java's item order, Q07 conflict-rounds, Q07 inside-out, seeded shuffle 1), each on its own clone of the post-fanout board, kept by (incomplete, router score, arm index) (Q12.1)

pairs_rule: amendment 1: the verdict pair is (mpdef, portfolio4), judged by the totals rule with guard_extra; (mp1, portfolio4) is reported (what the portfolio adds to pass 1); mp1 also decides `eligible`. Registered: baseline_arm/candidate_arm name the primary pair for freerouting-dev gate; every pair is judged on its own by the totals rule; a candidate passes only if it passes against mpdef (the portfolio replaces passes 2-10 at about their work) and meets guard_extra; its pair against mp1 is reported (what the portfolio adds to pass 1)

boards.eligibility: every board of tools/bench/sets/benchmark.txt, owner.txt and the 2-layer medium/hard rows of kicad-corpus.txt on which the unchanged engine at the registration commit (arm mp1) leaves at least one incomplete connection; the list goes into `eligible` below, as an amendment that changes nothing else, before any candidate arm runs. canary-pwr-9511d9a and pours1..3 count as one board (grouped, as in Q01.json).
boards.grouped: none since amendment 1 (one canary-pwr row, canary-pwr-9511d9a); registered: fixtures/canary-pwr/*.dsn are one board for pass_rule (the variants of one placement)
boards.board_flags: none beyond the arm commands; the canary-pwr flags are in every command (start_ripup_costs 1500, min_trace_width_um 150), as Q10.json and Q11.json use them. Threads (autorouter.max_threads) are the run host's: no result depends on them (Q12.1), only wall_seconds
boards.why: Q10's universe and eligibility rule: Q10, Q11 and Q12 are measured as one family (Q00), so they share the boards (the same files as Q11.json)

grading: tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh where a .kicad_pcb exists (copper severities forced to error, input DRC subtracted, refill on); canary-pwr by canary-23 (ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py)

metric_definitions.work_units: the run's maze work units (freerouting-dev bench record), summed over every portfolio arm and restart (each arm's work is done, whether its board is kept or not)
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.unrouted: the router's final unrouted count (its log)

extra_reported: order spread per board: min/median/max of unrouted over the 4 portfolio arms, from the job log's 'Portfolio:' line, and of kicad_unconnected where graded (Q12.4)
the kept arm per board (the job log's 'kept arm' index and label)
peak resident memory per board for the portfolio4 arm (Q12.3; amendment 1: /usr/bin/time's maximum resident set of the run, tools/bench/quick-arm.sh's .time file)
guard_extra: work_units at most 1.5x mpdef's on every board
keep_rule: amendment 1: keep portfolio4 as a setting (off by default, in no profile) only if it passes the totals rule against mpdef and meets guard_extra. Registered: keep the best passing candidate as a setting (off by default, in no profile) only if it passes the totals rule against mpdef and meets guard_extra; with several passing, the fewest kicad_unconnected summed over the eligible boards, ties by fewest work_units. A change to profile enhanced needs its own registration
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board after P04's default-tree decision; no reruns with other K, restarts, seeds, arm lists or memory limits
not_registered: arm lists other than Q12's fixed list
the portfolio with the default passes (portfolio without -mp 1)
amendment 1: the arms portfolio4+restart2 and portfolio4+Q10+Q11 (dropped: two arms where the question allows)

decision_table.pass: keep as a setting (off by default); DIVERGENCES line; Q12.4's spread table proposed to F03 as the per-board quantum
decision_table.fail: remove quality/portfolio/; the spread table stays in Q12.4's done note (it is a finding either way)

timing: measured only after P04's default-tree decision

amendments.after: the registration; before any registered run of any arm on any row (Q12.1-Q12.4's spot checks on canary-pwr-9511d9a and Issue433-my-board are not runs of this registration)
amendments.reason: decided 2026-10-20: measurement runs stay a few minutes: every row routes in well under a minute except canary-pwr's DSN, two arms where the question allows (here the verdict pair and the pass-1 baseline Q11 already runs), one KiCad grade per distinct session. The registered 5 arms on 30 rows would take hours
amendments.changes: (1) Rows: boards.files keeps the 15 rows of tools/bench/sets/q10-sweep-quick.txt, as Q11.json's amendment 1 (each row's longest recorded route time and its target/orchestrator/<dir>/ are in that file; canary-pwr-9511d9a's default passes took 414.4 to 451.7 s in n06-13 and n06-g, under the 600 s limit); dropped for their route time: bm01, CPU-85, z10_module, smoothieboard, LogicBoard_smt, GP8B, coldfire, contribution-board, the five canary-pwr variants, eprom-card-80bus and rio-iceshield. The eligibility rule and min_boards 3 are unchanged. (2) Arms: mpdef (baseline), portfolio4 (candidate) and mp1 (reported pair and eligibility), mp1's command equal to Q11.json's mp1 (plus --router.special.diagnostics=rip-stats, report-only) so its runs serve both; portfolio4+restart2 and portfolio4+Q10+Q11 are dropped. (3) Grading: one KiCad grade per distinct session; the 8 benchmark rows have no .kicad_pcb and use the router's unrouted count. Q12.3's peak resident memory is the portfolio4 run's /usr/bin/time maximum resident set (LogicBoard_smt is not a row: its fanout alone outlasts 170 s). (4) Every route runs under ulimit -v 8000000 with timeout 600 for canary-pwr-9511d9a and timeout 120 for the other rows; a timeout leaves the measurement incomplete. Nothing else changes: question, metrics, totals block, guard_extra, stop_rule

amendments.after: amendment 1; before any registered run of any arm on any row
amendments.reason: the run's engine, runner and grading made precise before any number (amendment 1 names 'main at the run' and the grade scripts, not the metric sources), with the hard-guard reading every measurement since N06.4 uses
amendments.changes: (1) Engine: amendment 1's 'main at the run' is main 3330f36 (freerouting --version: git 3330f369a2ab), one Linux release build of freerouting-cli and freerouting-dev from a detached worktree of that commit (CLI sha256 a6bc2d82eceaf406...), default profile enhanced, every arm. (2) Runner: tools/bench/quick-arm.sh, which adds --result-json (the result manifest) to each route, and every route also gets --stats json (output only: the per-stage counters next to the SES, for work_units); outputs in target/orchestrator/q1112/out/<arm>/<board>.*. (3) Grading made precise: canary-pwr-9511d9a through Q10's canary grade (target/orchestrator/q10/s104/canary-grade.sh with its WSL kicad-cli shim, canary 9511d9a3: ses_import.py, kicad-cli pcb drc --schematic-parity --refill-zones --severity-all, via_in_pad.py, inner_tracks.py): kicad_unconnected = unconnected items, drc_real = error items other than unconnected items and starved thermals, below_minimum_raw = track_width errors, via_in_pad_raw = via_in_pad.py's count; the corpus rows through tools/kicad-oracle/grade.sh on target/corpus/projects/<id> with the engine `cp <session> {SES}` (tools/bench/grade-distinct.sh): kicad_unconnected = unconnected_items, drc_real = drc_real, below_minimum_raw = the sum of copper.below_minimum; the benchmark rows: kicad_unconnected and drc_real null (a null pair is not compared), below_minimum_raw = the session's traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input does not have. On the benchmark and corpus rows via_in_pad_raw = added vias in SMD pads (main 4885a30's added_via_in_pad). Hard guards via_in_pad and below_minimum are 'no new breach versus baseline' (decided 2026-10-18: no registration carries a hard guard the baseline already breaks; the commands' 150 um floor with enhanced's neck-down breaks the raw KiCad track_width minimum in every arm, Q10.4): the arm's raw count minus the pair's baseline arm's raw count on the same row, floored at 0, so one records file per pair as rule_text says; the raw counts are reported in the done note. On every row: pour_lost_pins = quality::pour_audit::audit (input board against input + SES), vias and length_mm = the imported session's statistics, all three by a scratch tool on the engine API at the same commit (N06.13's n06m plus Q10's pour audit, target/orchestrator/q1112/q11m); unrouted = the result manifest's board_statistics.connections.incomplete_count (the log's final unrouted count) and connections = its maximum_count (the default noise band of rows without a registered band); work_units = maze_work_units of the --stats total; wall_seconds = /usr/bin/time's elapsed seconds (other sessions' routes and builds ran at the same time: reported, not compared). (4) Numbering: the `eligible` amendment that amendment 1's notes call amendment 2 is amendment 3. Written before any registered run of any arm on any row. Nothing else changes: arms, commands, rows, metrics, totals block, pairs, keep and stop rules The work_units sum covers every portfolio arm and the optimizer (the --stats total counts them all, checked on a scratch route of Issue433-my-board with portfolio 2, not a registered command).

amendments.after: mp1's registered runs; before any candidate arm runs
amendments.reason: the registration's eligibility rule: `eligible` is written as an amendment before any candidate arm runs
amendments.changes: eligible: the 11 rows on which mp1 (main 3330f36, amendment 2) left at least one incomplete connection, 11 distinct boards (all but Issue649-kicad_ecc83-pp_input_board_v1, Issue508-DAC2020_bm02, Issue508-DAC2020_bm07 and mccx11-hardware-sx1262-433mhz-reverse-engineering, complete under mp1); the verdicts are read on these rows (freerouting-dev gate --eligible), every registered row is still run and recorded. Written after mp1's runs (and Q11.1's sweep arms, which are not candidates) and before any candidate arm runs. Nothing else changes
